analysis:
Integration of all 12 units: the PR splits the CI test-provider route lane into five per-shard lanes (test-provider-1..5, count 1 each) in .github/workflows/ci.yml (route lanes at head lines 43-47; runs-on at head line 143 uses format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)). The matching docs (docs/developer/build.md, docs/developer/test.md) and the offline test scripts (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py) are updated to pin the per-shard lanes via the new SHARDED set, matrix_shards, job_lanes and requested_lanes helpers.

No provider runtime, coordinator contract, key custody, attestation, App Attest, prefix-cache (T-041), fan helper, add-on hold or sandbox-installer code is touched. The threat-model assets and boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013) are therefore unaffected.

The CI guardrails visible in the diff are preserved: the route job keeps permissions: {} and no secrets, workflow contents stays read, release/signing/publication/model-registration jobs keep literal Blacksmith labels, and fork PRs and exact-label matching are still tested. The format() argument comes from the static integer matrix [1..5], so there is no injection vector. The tests still assert a fallback for every requested lane.

Remaining unverified items, which are outside the supplied evidence and not demonstrated defects: darkbloom-route.yml and the sandbox plane's acceptance of the new lane names (a missing key would cause a CI failure or fallback, not a confidentiality or integrity regression), and the isolation of sandbox runners, which is unchanged by this PR. The integration replay was partial (29 units omitted), but the supplied patches show only CI-structure and doc changes. No finding qualifies.
